meta.title: Discovered Technology
meta.note: Every entry is a piece of technology the filings actually describe: what it is, where it was seen, which article saw it first and in what year. Quotes are verbatim from the source article and are checked by tools/check-technology.py. The tension figures are derived from this ledger, not authored; see docs/TECHNOLOGY_SYSTEM.md.

weapon.label: Weapon
weapon.blurb: Things built to hurt a person.

siege.label: Siege engine
siege.blurb: Things built to open a building that did not want opening.

vehicle.label: Vehicle
vehicle.blurb: Things that move people, and sometimes stop moving them.

communications.label: Signals
communications.blurb: Radios, telephones and the voices that arrive over them.

construct.label: Construct
construct.blurb: Machines that move on their own.

magitek.label: Magitek
magitek.blurb: Engineering that runs on something the Guild would like to regulate.

medical.label: Medical
medical.blurb: Things that put people back together, on someone's terms.

infrastructure.label: Infrastructure
infrastructure.blurb: Roads, lines, presses and pipes: the things a territory runs on.

tiers.name: Age of Iron
tiers.blurb: Steel, codified magic, and roads nobody can see.

tiers.name: Industrial Era
tiers.blurb: Engines, airframes, radio and mass production.

tiers.name: Cosmic Era
tiers.blurb: Salvage from elsewhere: drones, reactors and planar hardware.

eastern_midlands.name: The Eastern Midlands (contested)
eastern_midlands.blurb: Raventree ground outside the Mushroom Kingdom and short of the Empire: nobody's atlas page, everybody's problem.

meta.pressureScale: -3 (settles a territory) to +3 (arms it). Authored per entry from what the filing shows the thing doing; the board multiplies it by a recency weight and sums it per territory.

bands.name: Cycle of Calm
bands.blurb: Tools and medicine outnumber weapons on the record.

bands.name: Cycle of Discovery
bands.blurb: New things on the record and nobody shooting yet.

bands.name: Cycle of Tension
bands.blurb: Arms are on the ground and the filings say who is pointing them.

bands.name: Cycle of Conflict
bands.blurb: Weapons have been used in the territory this cycle.

bands.name: Cycle of Crisis
bands.blurb: Siege machinery, artillery or planar hardware in play.

entries.name: Wario's Transport Helicopter

territory.label: Waluigi's Outpost to Star Hill, Mushroom Kingdom interior

origin.maker: Wario Enterprise fleet

sightings.note: Flown by Wario himself after the pilot was fired at altitude; tripped on the storehouse parapet beside Dr. Toad's clinic and rolled onto its side, burning.

entries.status: Wrecked - on its side on the storehouse roof at Star Hill, inside the pipe fire, red light still going
entries.summary: A rotor transport with a searchlight, a loudhailer and an underbelly that opens: the machine Wario answered a balcony reading with, and the machine he later put on a roof.
entries.record: The helicopter arrived at the outpost ahead of its own noise, flattened the archivist's coat with downdraft and opened the negotiation through a loudhailer. Two weeks of silence ended with it hovering over a patio. On the Star Hill leg Wario flew it himself, the pilot dismissed by bulldog clip and stowed in the rear hold, and the one person aboard who knew what the yellow light meant was not in the cockpit. The skid caught a parapet, the main rotor met a chimney stack, and the last blade rang on the cobbles of the clinic street.

quotes.text: The shape lifted off the peak and resolved into rotors and a searchlight, and the searchlight was not sweeping the valley.
There is a pilot in the rear hold of this helicopter, fired by bulldog clip, and he is the only person aboard who knows what the yellow light means.
The helicopter did not fall; it was *tripped*.

tension.why: A private transport flown by its owner into a Regency-protected clinic street, and left burning on a roof beside it.

entries.name: The W-Stamped Mechanical Claw

territory.label: Waluigi's Outpost - the patio and the study door

origin.maker: Wario Enterprise (owner-operated, housing stamped with a single W)

entries.status: In service - last seen taking the Contract of Accord off a balcony with the delicacy of a pickpocket
entries.summary: A reinforced claw arm that drops from the helicopter's underbelly, with a smaller pincer for the fine work; it was used on a scholar's door over a 14,783-gold invoice.
entries.record: The underbelly opened and delivered the evening's thesis: a yellow-and-black claw on a reinforced arm, scaled like a drawbridge winch, with a W painted on the housing. It struck the study door four times, got caught in an Ice Storm, and ticked as its joints cooled. A second, smaller pincer worked the upper crack wider while the big one was frozen. The same arm later took the signed page with a care that frightened the archivist more than the four strikes had.

quotes.text: A mechanical claw on a reinforced arm — yellow and black, scaled like a drawbridge winch, and painted on its housing, in case posterity should wonder whose fist was coming through a scholar's door at midnight, a single enormous 'W'.
A smaller claw — pincers, delicate, horrible — poked through a crack higher up and snapped at the air, tasting the room.
The great claw took the page with a delicacy that frightened me more than the four strikes had — pincers like a surgeon who moonlights as a pickpocket.

tension.why: Siege machinery deployed from the air against a private residence inside the Kingdom over an invoice.

entries.name: The Enterprise Field Radio

territory.label: Waluigi's Outpost - the landing platform

origin.maker: Wario Enterprise

sightings.note: The informant's 'private wing, high security, consciousness fluxing' arrived over this set and was never checked against anything.

entries.status: In service - the only source for the Star Hill lockdown report
entries.summary: The hand-set Wario barks REPORT into; it chose the next destination of the whole arc on the word of a paid informant.
entries.record: The radio supplied the next problem before the ink on the accord was dry: Star Hill Clinic locked down, Luigi inside, medical complications. Everything the pair knew about the clinic that night came through this set, relayed by a creditor who profits from urgency. The archive files it as a piece of technology because it decided where the helicopter went.

quotes.text: The radio then supplied the next problem: Star Hill Clinic is reportedly locked down, with Luigi inside.
The Star Hill lockdown is radio chatter from a paid informant, relayed by a creditor who profits from urgency.

tension.why: Unverified radio chatter about a Regency-protected clinic moved an armed party toward it.

entries.name: A Courier's Cheap Pistol

territory.label: Star Hill - the clinic's main street and the storehouse stairwell

origin.maker: Unknown - cheap, and it jams

entries.status: With Paulo - jammed twice on the record, cleared or replaced once, last fired into a rotor blade a hand's width from Waluigi's ear
entries.summary: The pistol that came out of a courier's satchel when a man in green would not get off the route, and that clicked in Waluigi's face on the stairs.
entries.record: Paulo drew it in the street on the thing reciting at him, and it was the first shot of the night. On the stairwell it came round the newel post before he did and stopped a hand's width from Waluigi's face; it clicked, and the bluff about one per cent of capacity held exactly as long as a cheap pistol takes to jam. In the street afterwards a second pistol, or the same one cleared, took the lip off the fallen rotor blade beside Waluigi's ear and put him on the cobbles.

quotes.text: The courier's hand came out of the satchel holding a pistol.
The pistol clicked.
He had a second pistol, or the same one cleared, and this time he did not put it in Waluigi's face.

tension.why: Gunfire in a clinic street in the Kingdom, between a courier and the pair who had just crashed on the roof.

entries.name: The WarioWare Tower Brass Telephone

territory.label: WarioWare Tower, Toad Town

origin.maker: WarioWare executive fittings

entries.status: On the executive desk
entries.summary: The heavy desk set Wario snatched up to raise the four-call squad before the embassy ambush.
entries.record: Mobilisation for the Mage's Embassy began with a receiver torn from its cradle. The archive keeps the telephone on the ledger because the whole ambush was assembled over it, call by call, before anyone left the tower.

quotes.text: Wario marched directly to the heavy brass telephone on his executive desk, snatching the receiver from its cradle.

tension.why: The ambush on the Mage's Embassy was raised over this line.

entries.name: The Fawthful Drone

territory.label: Bowser's Castle - the rooms beyond the throne room

origin.maker: Fawful's workshop

entries.status: Loose in the castle
entries.summary: A small drone of Fawful's make that turned up in the room after the throne-room breach and found a remnant force that no longer knew which destination belonged to the king.
entries.record: It appeared in the next room while the breach was still being argued over, and a Goomba walked toward it. The archive notes that nobody in the room asked who was watching through it.

quotes.text: A small Fawthful drone appeared in the next room.
The Goomba walked toward the Fawthful drone.

tension.why: Fawful's eyes inside Bowser's castle during a breach.

entries.name: Green T's Birthday Musket

territory.label: Shadeward Manor, the Shadow Estate (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: Unknown - a gift from Green T

entries.status: Confiscated - Green T gave it, watched it used as a lever on a wall climb, and kept it
entries.summary: A blackpowder long gun given to Remi for her birthday and taken back the same night after it was used as a climbing lever.
entries.record: The musket entered the record as a present and left it as evidence of what presents are for. Remi used it as a lever on the exterior wall; Green T held it out, pulled her to safety with it, and then looked at the thing in his hands and did not give it back.

quotes.text: Green T gave Remi a Wario-themed garlic grenade and a musket as birthday gifts and then took the musket back.
He held the musket out, pulled it back with Remi hanging from it, brought her to safety, and then looked at the musket in his hands and kept it.

entries.name: The Wario-Themed Garlic Grenade

territory.label: Shadeward Manor, the Shadow Estate (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: Wario-branded - provenance of the branding unrecorded

entries.status: Given to Remi - not yet thrown on any filing
entries.summary: A hand-thrown garlic device with Wario's branding on it, given as a birthday present in the Shadowfell.
entries.record: Of the two birthday gifts only the grenade stayed with its recipient. The archive lists it because a Wario-branded explosive turning up in a Shadowfell manor is a supply line, and supply lines are filed.

quotes.text: Green T gave Remi a Wario-themed garlic grenade and a musket as birthday gifts and then took the musket back.

tension.why: Wario-branded ordnance circulating on Corvinarus-adjacent ground.

entries.name: The Corvinarus Sanctum Telescope

territory.label: Corvinarus Sanctum - the clockwork observatory and telescope platforms (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: The Corvinarus Sanctum's clockwork observatory

entries.status: In place - it shows the viewer something, and what it showed Bowser he called 'something sad'
entries.summary: A telescope on a platform in a collapsing clockwork observatory; Bowser looked through it and came away hurt.
entries.record: The party reached a telescope platform inside the sanctum. Bowser looked, pulled away, called the vision something sad, and kept walking. The archive files the instrument rather than the vision: what it shows is unverified, but the fact that it shows is on the record.

quotes.text: They reached a telescope platform.
The telescope hurt Bowser.

entries.name: Bowser's Portable Bullet Bill Cannon

territory.label: Raventree Manor and the Fracture Grove - Eastern Midlands, contested ground

origin.maker: Koopa Troop ordnance

entries.status: Carried by Bowser - produced from his shell
entries.summary: A shell-carried Bullet Bill launcher that Bowser produced in the Grove of Woe and patted.
entries.record: Bowser emerged from his shell and produced a portable Bullet Bill cannon, in capitals, because the archivist was there. It is the heaviest piece of ordnance filed on Raventree ground and it was being carried by a king who had fallen through a midnight portal a month earlier by Shadowfell reckoning.

quotes.text: Bowser emerged from his shell and produced a portable Bullet Bill cannon.
He patted the Bullet Bill cannon.

tension.why: Koopa artillery carried onto Corvinarus-contested ground.
Heavy ordnance inside a Guild-watched fracture site.

entries.name: The Kitchen Device That Could Close Every Portal

territory.label: Ruined Raventree Manor - the portal kitchen approaches

origin.maker: Unknown - described by Agent L (Luigi) inside the Mages Guild room

entries.status: Unverified - described, not seen; the largest unexamined decision in the session was waved through in four lines
entries.summary: A device in the manor kitchen that, by Luigi's casual account, could close the portals connecting the manor to the other planes entirely.
entries.record: Once weapons were lowered, the conversation turned with startling casualness to a kitchen device capable of permanently trapping an unknown number of people on a plane with no way home. Luigi's risk reading was that it would never happen. The archive files the device at the top of the magitek ledger because the thing it would do is the largest thing anything on this list would do.

quotes.text: Once weapons were lowered, the conversation turned immediately, and with startling casualness, to something enormous: a device in the kitchen that could close the portals connecting this location to other planes entirely.

tension.why: A portal-closing device sitting in a manor whose other side is the Shadowfell.

entries.name: Agent L's Vacuum Device

territory.label: Ruined Raventree Manor - a side room off the portal kitchen

origin.maker: Unknown - carried by Luigi as Agent L

entries.status: Carried by Agent L - pressed to a face once, then lowered
entries.summary: The vacuum device Luigi pressed to Ryan's face before he recognised him.
entries.record: Ryan entered a room and was tackled, and a vacuum device was on his face before Agent L recognised him and let go. The archive lists it as a device rather than a weapon because nobody has filed what it does when the trigger is pulled on something that is not a friend.

quotes.text: Entering a room, Ryan was tackled and had a vacuum device pressed to his face before Agent L — Luigi — recognized him and let go.

entries.name: The Iron Legion Field Syringe

territory.label: The Skittering Grove, Shadow Estate grounds (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: Iron Legion field issue

entries.status: Legion issue - used on Eager in the grove
entries.summary: The syringe a Legion guard used on Eager after telling him to stand still; the archive files it as the Legion's procedure made physical.
entries.record: The Legion closed the night by closing its own loop: a guard told a wounded man to stand still and got out a syringe. Whatever was in it worked on Eager. The archivist files it as that sentence made physical - an institution that processes fear, and wounds, and objections, through procedure.

quotes.text: One got out a syringe.
He files the syringe now as that sentence made physical: an institution that processes fear, and wounds, and objections, through procedure.

tension.why: Legion field medicine applied to a man who asked to be put down, on the Legion's terms.

entries.name: The Legion Airlift That Never Came

territory.label: The Skittering Grove, Shadow Estate grounds (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: Iron Legion - promised, not produced

entries.status: Unverified - nothing in the record shows one
entries.summary: A helicopter the Legion guards promised to a burning grove; Dan asked what a helicopter was; none arrived.
entries.record: The word airlift entered the grove as reassurance and left it as a description of what was promised. A Toad who had never heard of a helicopter asked what one was. The archive files the absence: a piece of technology that exists in the Legion's sentences and nowhere else on this record.

quotes.text: Not to worry — we have a helicopter to airlift us all out of here.
The word *airlift* describes what was promised, not what happened.

tension.why: A promised extraction that did not come, to Toads who were told to wait for it.

entries.name: The Director's Wired Remote

territory.label: The Nintendo Mania studio - the dark hallway past the maintenance room

origin.maker: Unknown - carried by the Director with the ease of long habit

entries.status: In the Director's hand - the archive's standing thought is that it could be the key to stopping everything
entries.summary: A small control unit with buttons and wires running from it, carried by the Director; the studio appears to run off it.
entries.record: Darian, alone, watched the Director pass in a dark hallway with a folder in one hand and in the other a small remote device with buttons and wires running from it. A control unit. The filing ends on the thought the archive cannot put down: that the remote could stop everything, if they can get it.

quotes.text: In the other, carried with the ease of long habit, a **small remote device with buttons and wires running from it.**
that remote could be the key to stopping everything — if they can get it.

entries.name: The EMERGENCY EXIT Coffee Machine

territory.label: The Nintendo Mania studio - the break room

origin.maker: Studio fittings

entries.status: Shut off by Alistair after it had done its work on the ceiling
entries.summary: A button labelled EMERGENCY EXIT beside a coffee machine; pressing it made coffee, and the steam popped the ceiling vent that became the actual exit.
entries.record: Darian pressed the EMERGENCY EXIT button and got coffee. The scalding pot and the steam opened a ceiling vent, and the escape went up instead of out. The archive keeps it on the ledger as the studio's most honest piece of engineering: it did exactly what it said, by accident.

quotes.text: Darian presses the EMERGENCY EXIT button and gets coffee — until the steam pops a ceiling vent open, and the escape goes up instead of out.

entries.name: The Regal Empire Military Airship

territory.label: Swiftsoul Keep - the upper-level airship docks, Regal Empire

origin.maker: Regal Empire military shipyards

entries.status: Docked under heavy guard at Swiftsoul Keep
entries.summary: A state-of-the-art military airship at the Keep's guarded docks - the transport the party was trying to reach when it became internationally wanted.
entries.record: The party went to Swiftsoul Keep looking for transport out of the region via the military airship docks. What was docked there was a state-of-the-art, military-grade Regal Empire airship, in the pristine upper levels beside the Royal military command and the magistrates' courts. The arc ended with the party as fugitives and the ship still the Empire's.

quotes.text: A state-of-the-art, military-grade Regal Empire airship.
They were heading to Swiftsoul Keep, specifically seeking transport out of the region via the heavily guarded military airship docks.

tension.why: Military airlift capacity concentrated at the Empire's border keep.

entries.name: The Maglev Express

territory.label: Blackwood Junction and the line to the Clockwork Spire, Mushroom Kingdom

origin.maker: Mages' Guild transport

firstSeen.date: Night of Departure - approximately 11:42 PM, three days before the Clockwork Spire (963 BF)

sightings.note: The expedition it was carrying reached the Guild District on Chillwind 8, 963 BF.

entries.status: Running - after all five pulled the lever
entries.summary: A Mages' Guild magnetic-levitation train with a Research & Logistics car and a Main Control Hub that answers to one large lever marked FORWARD.
entries.record: The Main Control Hub is the structural brain of the Maglev Express: a single large lever among unresponsive buttons and flickering dials. Five people pulled it. The archive files the train as infrastructure rather than vehicle because the line it runs on decides where the Guild can send people, and when.

quotes.text: The Main Control Hub is the structural brain of the Maglev Express.
A single large lever prominently positioned among unresponsive buttons and flickering dials.
Well, might as well flip this lever that says FORWARD.

entries.name: Cleaning Golem Patrol Unit 7

territory.label: Sublevel Three maintenance tunnels, Guild District, Mushroom Kingdom

origin.maker: Guild District automated maintenance

entries.status: Decommissioned - precision hydraulic valve extraction by a trainee on his first deployment
entries.summary: A multi-ton automated construct running at degraded Long Dark capacity, blinded with a spectral flare and taken apart in under ninety seconds.
entries.record: The group bypassed a checkpoint through the Sublevel Three tunnels and met Cleaning Golem Patrol Unit 7. Leo blinded its optical sensors with the Prototype-X's spectral flare and disabled it by pulling the right hydraulic valve, which E. Gadd filed as considerably exceeding expectations. The archive files the golem as the Guild District's security on the day the District was failing.

quotes.text: Cleaning Golem Patrol Unit 7 decommissioned in Sublevel Three via precision hydraulic valve extraction by a trainee on his first deployment.

entries.name: Bowser's Koopa Clown Car

territory.label: Bowser's Castle roof, Valley of Bowser

origin.maker: Koopa Troop

entries.status: Parked on the castle roof as of 955 BF
entries.summary: The king's personal flying machine, seen by lightning on the castle roof three weeks after the assassination.
entries.record: The lightning that lights the valley's cavern sky showed the Clown Car's silhouette on the castle roof and then took it away again. Toadsmith considered it. The archive files it as the oldest personal aircraft on the ledger.

quotes.text: The lightning that perpetually illuminates the valley's cavern sky flashed in the background, briefly revealing the silhouette of Bowser's Koopa Clown Car on the castle roof before darkness swallowed it again.

entries.name: The Donut Plains Warp Pipe

territory.label: The valley floor below Bowser's Castle, marked for Donut Plains

origin.maker: Unknown - older than every faction on the ledger

entries.status: Working - the spiral tile glows when a foot touches it
entries.summary: A half-buried, vine-covered pipe with the yellow-and-blue spiral of Donut Plains, at the end of a maintenance trail out of the valley.
entries.record: At the trail's end sat a warp pipe entrance, half-buried in dirt and covered in vines, marked with the Donut Plains spiral. The tile glowed faintly when Toadsmith's foot touched it. The archive files pipes as infrastructure: whoever maps them owns the roads nobody can see.

quotes.text: And at the trail's end: a warp pipe entrance, half-buried in dirt, covered in vines, marked with the yellow-and-blue spiral pattern of Donut Plains.

entries.name: The Royal Capital Printing Press

territory.label: The print shop, Mushroom Kingdom Royal Capital

origin.maker: Royal Capital print shop

entries.status: Working, slowly - 575 pamphlets
entries.summary: A single slow press that printed the 575 pamphlets in the days after the assassination.
entries.record: Toadsworth was present for the press and the 575 pamphlets. The archive files it because the first thing a capital reaches for after a killing is a way to say so in quantity, and this one said so slowly.

quotes.text: A single slow printing press.
Toadsworth was present for the subsequent events — the printing press, the 575 pamphlets.

entries.name: Crashed Shroob Technology (the Regal Magitek Salvage)

territory.label: Proto-Regal Empire borders and the north-west Mushroom Kingdom rifts

origin.maker: Shroob - reverse-engineered by the Proto-Regal Empire

firstSeen.date: Chronological present 950 BF; chronological past 840 BF

entries.status: Absorbed - it is the root of the Empire's modern Magitek arsenal
entries.summary: Salvage from the Shroob incursion, secured in the past by the Proto-Regal Empire and reverse-engineered into the Magitek the Empire fields today.
entries.record: Waluigi watched the incursion, took the temporal arbitrage, and watched the early Empire use crashed Shroob technology to jumpstart its Magitek arsenal. It is all reverse-engineered Shroob technology. The Empire secured enough of it in the past to guarantee its future and did not want anyone going back to contest the salvage claims.

quotes.text: It is all reverse-engineered Shroob technology.

The Proto-Regal Empire (which was rapidly becoming the modern Regal Empire) had secured enough Shroob technology in the past to guarantee their future dominance, and they did not want anyone going back to contest their salvage claims.

tension.why: The Empire's arsenal rests on salvage taken from rifts on the Kingdom's north-west border.

entries.name: The Star Sprite Reactor

territory.label: Iron Shmolder's cave system - Star Sprite territory and the lava caverns

origin.maker: Star Sprites - connected to the star shard

entries.status: Powering up at last report - connected to the star shard
entries.summary: A reactor the Star Sprites were powering up, connected to the star shard, that a Hammer Bro's unit had been sent to interrupt.
entries.record: The Hammer Bro explained his situation: his unit was supposed to ambush the Star Sprites powering up a reactor connected to the star shard, and Fawful had imprisoned him because Fawful operated on his own agenda. The archive files the reactor without a year because the record does not have one.

quotes.text: Their defensive preparations — powering up a reactor, attempting to summon something bigger — were proportional to the threat.

tension.why: A Koopa patrol sent against the reactor was imprisoned by Fawful on his own agenda.

entries.name: The Mount Ebott Survey Machine

territory.label: Snowdin Town, the Monster Underground, Mount Ebott

origin.maker: Survey instrument - repaired to a 98-percent state by Flowey

entries.status: Running - 'Functioning normally' - with its data chip extracted and in the Agent's keeping
entries.summary: An abandoned survey machine that fixed itself, or was fixed by a flower; the Agent kicked it, then pulled its data chip.
entries.record: Spotting someone near the abandoned survey machine, the Agent, Mihawk and Sans gave chase. The machine came back reading Functioning normally, and the Agent extracted the data chip - the one portable piece of evidence that can later be compared against the damaged packet, the 98-percent repair state and any future scan. Both factions left with reasons to distrust the next report.

quotes.text: The Agent extracted the data chip.
The Agent authorized himself as his own commanding officer to justify kicking a machine.

tension.why: A Legion-named survey instrument, a flower who repairs it, and a data chip neither side trusts.

entries.name: The Radio That Graded Them First

territory.label: Helicopter crash site at the tree line outside the Schoolhouse perimeter - ground unplaced on the atlas

origin.maker: Regency field issue - Operation POP QUIZ

firstSeen.date: Operation POP QUIZ - timestamps corrupted inside the perimeter; estimated within the first ninety days after the 955 BF assassination

entries.status: Compromised - it answers before you ask
entries.summary: A Regency field radio that, when Ghost tried to raise Command from the crash site, returned a glitching whisper saying 'Correct answer' before anyone had answered anything.
entries.record: Ghost came to in the tilted cockpit with cracked ribs, found Brick unconscious in the troop compartment, and tried the radio. What came back was not Command. The archive files the set because a radio that grades you before you transmit is not a radio any more, and the Regency sent people in behind it.

quotes.text: The radio attempt produced not Command but a distorted glitchy whisper from everywhere and nowhere saying 'Correct answer' — before Ghost and Brick had answered anything.

tension.why: A Regency insertion against a site that has opinions about time, run on signals the Regency did not control.

entries.name: The Vacuum Shroom

territory.label: Fawful's Bean Badge, Toad Town — explained at the counter at dawn; built for Peach's Castle

origin.maker: Fawful — his own make, by the account: Fawful tech

firstSeen.date: Efferd, 955 BF — dawn, in the shop; not yet used

entries.status: Explained, not used — the last account has it in Fawful's hand and the vial in the Koopa's
entries.summary: A mushroom of Fawful's making that, inhaled, turns the inhaler into a vacuum: Bowser breathes it and sucks up everything in reach, the Mario brothers included. The dose was to reach him through the Koopa prisoner's fat vial, with the castle's wards still active.
entries.record: Fawful put on a Mages' Guild cloak to explain it, in his own shop, to a ceremonial guard who had been shot at by the people whose cloak it was. The archive files the shroom as described and not one word further, because the account does not see it used; what it sees is a plan with a mushroom in it, a vial to carry the mushroom, and two Guild operatives who did not correct the pronoun when Fawful said he would take over the kingdom. A device that makes the Koopa King inhale the heroes is the kind of thing the Highsun 1 record would explain very neatly, and the archive distrusts neatness.

quotes.text: The vacuum shroom — Fawful's own make, the account says, Fawful tech — which, inhaled, turns the inhaler into a vacuum: Bowser breathes it and sucks up everything in reach, the brothers included.
The Koopa had a fat vial — the account calls it that, the fat vial, a glass thing with weight in it — and the shroom was to go into Bowser by way of it.

tension.why: A device built to be fed to the Koopa King so that he swallows his own enemies for somebody else's benefit.
The Guild lent the cloak the plan was explained in, and a month later Bowser was the official murderer.

entries.name: The Guild's Small Orb

territory.label: The hall of Peach's Castle — held up by one Mages' Guild hood, once

origin.maker: Mages' Guild — pattern unknown; nothing the archive holds from the Guild in 1040 BF resembles it

firstSeen.date: Efferd, 955 BF — the hall, after Bowser's fire

entries.status: Seen working once — one use, one Koopa King on the floor; not seen since
entries.summary: A hand-sized orb held up, not thrown, by a Mages' Guild member in the hall of Peach's Castle: Bowser went down at once, as a thing goes down when what was holding it up has been switched off. The Toads cheered.
entries.record: The archive files what it is shown working, and this was shown working on Bowser, in front of a hall of witnesses, to applause. One object, one use, one result. It is on the ledger because the Highsun 1 record has Bowser beaten in a corridor of the same castle a month later and dragged away unconscious, and because the thing that put him down this night belonged to the people who had been shaking a Koopa's hand in the dungeon twenty minutes before. The archive has no name for it and has not given it one.

quotes.text: A Mages' Guild member ended it. The account is clear that it was one hood, one object — a small orb, held up, not thrown — and that Bowser went down.
One shot. The Koopa King on the floor of Peach's Castle with his fire still smoking in the walls.

tension.why: One orb, one Koopa King down, and a hall of Toads learning to cheer the Guild.

entries.name: Wario's Motorbike

territory.label: The Skittering Grove, Shadow Estate grounds (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: Wario (WarioWare stock, by every sign)

sightings.note: Stalled in the undergrowth of the grove battlefield while the Scorncrow escaped in smoke and crow-feathers.
Markop's first ride: into the trees, then into Salam. Then the sentry post — Salam and a Legion guard posted on it with a bow.
Revved at the stump while the party ran from it; left an ettercap in the dust — the machine's first useful act since it hit a tree.

entries.status: At the stump with Markop; Wario on the far side of a passage
entries.summary: Wario's motorbike, left behind when Wario went through Anamatar's passage, rammed into a tree by a centaur on his first ride, used as a sentry post, and finally revved at the stump hard enough to leave an ettercap in the dust.
entries.record: The archive has filed this machine stalled, crashed and sat on before it filed it moving. On the grove floor Markop stood at the stump the plan was built around, watched the party run from it, and revved; Salam fired from the saddle; the bike left an ettercap behind. It is the only piece of the sentry arrangement, apart from the man on it, that did what it was for.

quotes.text: He stayed. He revved the motorbike.
Markop revved again and left an ettercap in the dust, which the archive files as the machine's first useful act since it hit a tree.

tension.why: The sentry post the Legion was asked to share, and then was not on the record for.

entries.name: The Electric Sphere

territory.label: The Skittering Grove, Shadow Estate grounds (Shadowfell)

origin.maker: Unknown — charged, the record says, by Archie Miser's electric magic during the giant battle

entries.status: Carried out of the grove by Eager, on two hit points
entries.summary: A sphere that hums, picked up by Eager at the end of the grove floor fight; the record says it was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic. The archive has no earlier sighting and files the claim as stated.
entries.record: The archive would prefer a provenance. It has a sentence: the sphere was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic. Archie's lightning is on the record elsewhere - the electric spear at the door, the strikes the Shadow Estate account calls significant because they were not fire - and the giant battle is on the record; a sphere charged in it is not. It surfaced when a scout with two hit points had a reason to pick it up. The entry is filed with the gap stated and a lead opened in the arc file.

quotes.text: Somewhere in this Eager picked up the electric sphere — the record says it was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic, and the archive has no earlier sighting of the thing and says so.

tension.why: A charged arcane object leaving a grove in a scout's hands, with a Guild warrant already on the man whose magic charged it.

entries.name: The Cottage Swipe-and-Release System

territory.label: An unnamed cottage; neither the site nor its operator is identified.

origin.maker: Unknown — the swipe reader and emergency release are described, but no maker is named.

firstSeen.date: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — estimated; start hour unknown

entries.status: Bones pressed the emergency release once; it opened every door. Power source, reset state, and current lock status are unknown.
entries.summary: A key swipe failed, then a single emergency-release button unlocked all doors in the cottage.
entries.record: The access system is known only through two actions: Bones tried a key swipe and the door stayed locked; the emergency-release button then opened every locked door. The account does not say what the swipe credential was, who installed the system, or whether the button reset after use. The model is a schematic of the button, not a reconstruction of the cottage.

quotes.text: Bones tried the key swipe. It failed; the door stayed locked.
He pressed it. The locks opened. Not just the one in front of him—all the doors.

entries.name: Fawful’s Hypno-Helmet Drone — 1040 Report

territory.label: Unnamed cottage/compound in the Material Plane; the route and region are not recorded.

origin.maker: Attributed to Fawful in Bones’s account; workshop and construction are not documented.

firstSeen.date: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — estimated; start hour unknown

entries.status: The drone escaped after the helmet was removed; its location and condition are unknown.
entries.summary: A drone tackled an unnamed person, forced a hypno-helmet over them, and lashed vines at Bones.
entries.record: Bones’s 2 Aethel report describes a device that combines a moving drone, a helmet, and mechanical vines. The account says it began eating the unnamed victim’s brain, but supplies no medical outcome; that claim is preserved as witness wording rather than independently verified anatomy. It is distinct from the surveillance drone filed from Bowser’s Castle in 1035: no record ties the two machines together.

quotes.text: A Fawful hypno-helmet drone tackled an unnamed person.
The drone's vines lashed at Bones.

entries.name: Fawful’s Clockwork Mustard Drone — 1040 Report

territory.label: Fawful-aligned compound/woodland; no location or route is established.

origin.maker: Fawful’s forces are attributed in the report; the actual builder is unknown.

firstSeen.date: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — estimated; start hour unknown

entries.status: Used in the pursuit; no recovery, destruction, or current location is recorded.
entries.summary: A separate clockwork drone sprayed mustard at Bones during Fawful’s pursuit.
entries.record: A second machine appears during the sacrifice preparations. Bones’s account distinguishes it from the hypno-helmet device: Fawful winds this one up, and it sprays mustard in the pursuit. The archive does not give its model, fuel, range, or final condition. The existing Mustard Sprayer in the Fawful-force roster is not assumed to be this device.

quotes.text: Fawful wound up a separate clockwork drone.
It spat mustard across the passage and across Bones.

entries.name: The “Archie Bot” at the Goblin Camp — 1040 Report

territory.label: Unnamed goblin camp in the Material Plane; site and region are not established.

origin.maker: Unknown — the camp calls the figure an “Archie bot”; construction and operator are unverified.

firstSeen.date: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — estimated; start hour unknown

entries.status: Observed using a water trick and speaking at the camp; the later dragon passenger may be the same figure, but the record does not establish that. No identity match to Archie Miser is made.
entries.summary: A camp figure called an “Archie bot” extinguished a fire with “WATERBALL!” and was recruited by the goblins.
entries.record: The ledger records the camp’s name for the figure and the action Bones observed. The event does not establish whether “bot” is a literal mechanical description, a title, or a joke. The schematic model is not a portrait. The dragon later leaves with an Archie-like passenger; the source does not establish that the bot and passenger are the same entity, and neither is merged with Archie Miser.

quotes.text: When the goblins lit a fire, a figure they called an Archie bot stood near it.
WATERBALL!
